pathway.title: WHIRLPOOL CORP /DE/ — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage has moved sharply the wrong way. Total debt over ongoing EBITDA was 5.43x in FY2024, 6.11x in FY2025 and is 9.52x for the twelve months to September 30, 2026, with net debt over ongoing EBITDA of 7.98x. On the stricter operating-profit basis the latest ratios are 8.46x and 7.10x, so the conclusion does not depend on which EBITDA is used. Total debt rose by USD 332 million over the first nine months of 2026 while ongoing EBITDA fell from USD 1,067 million in FY2025 to USD 720 million for the latest twelve months. The issuer does not print a leverage ratio, so every ratio here is analyst-built.

The refinancing bought time and cost carry. The June 2026 issue of USD 1,000 million of 7.500% notes due 2031 and USD 1,000 million of 7.875% notes due 2034 carries about USD 154 million of annual coupon (derived from the stated rates), replacing euro notes with coupons of 1.25% and 1.10% on about USD 1,290 million of carrying value, so roughly USD 139 million of added annual coupon before any saving on the repaid revolver. Quarterly interest expense reached USD 102 million in Q3 2026 against USD 63 million in Q2, and management guides full-year 2026 interest of about USD 350 million and Q4 interest of about USD 103 million. Ongoing EBITDA over annualised Q3 interest of USD 408 million is 1.76x, and guided full-year 2026 ongoing EBIT of about USD 293 million is 0.84x guided interest. Cash interest is not printed for the interim periods, so these are expense-based.

Liquidity is adequate on paper and uncertain in substance. Cash of USD 1,103 million and undrawn commitments of USD 2,193 million total USD 3,296 million, down from USD 4,101 million at December 31, 2025, and the nominal undrawn amount is mostly an ABL (USD 2,000 million) limited by a borrowing base the filings do not disclose. Operating cash flow was negative USD 826 million for nine months and management's guidance of about USD 700 million for the year implies a fourth-quarter inflow of about USD 1,526 million. That is a seasonal working capital release, not a trend, and it carries execution risk.

Covenant headroom is thin on every proxy available. The ABL tests fixed charge coverage of 1.00x only when Availability falls below the greater of 10% of the Line Cap and USD 135 million. An indicative proxy of ongoing EBITDA less capital expenditures over interest expense is 0.97x, so if availability tightened the test could bind. The proxy is not the covenant definition. The prior facility's interest coverage test of at least 3.0x was relaxed in May 2026 by excluding the first quarter, and expense-based cover has since fallen to 2.21x.

Creditor ranking has shifted. The ABL is first lien and the Secured Notes are second lien on the same collateral pool, secured by substantially all assets of the Company and the guarantors, while about USD 4.8 billion of senior unsecured notes (derived as total debt less the Secured Notes and notes payable) remain. Whether the unsecured note indentures allowed the lien grant or required equal and ratable security is not stated and the documents are not supplied. This is an open legal question, not an adverse finding.

Claims outside reported debt are material in aggregate. Supply chain finance of USD 650 million sits in payables, operating lease liabilities of USD 863 million noncurrent, a USD 575 million cumulative mandatory convertible preferred, Brazilian tax assessments (BEFIEX about USD 545 million, PIS/COFINS about USD 88 million, IPI Amnesty about USD 61 million, and USD 112 million unreserved for DIFAL), and USD 578 million of bank guarantees, letters of credit and surety bonds. None is in total debt.

cells.text: "Whirlpool manufactures and markets a full line of major home appliances and related products." Principal products are laundry, refrigerators and freezers, cooking and dishwashers, plus small domestic appliances (KitchenAid) and commercial laundry.
Durable, replacement-driven categories, but discretionary spend and housing activity drive volume, so operating leverage on fixed manufacturing cost magnifies downturns.
Three segments: MDA North America, MDA Latin America, SDA Global. Nine months 2026 net sales were 7,141, 2,500 and 710 respectively, with 116 in Other, out of 10,467 total.
North America dominates sales, so North American demand and tariff costs set group earnings and debt service capacity.
Nine months 2026 net sales by category: laundry 3,129, refrigeration 3,057, cooking 2,490, dishwashing 809, spare parts and warranties 404, other 579.
Spare parts, warranties and InSinkErator-type sales are a smaller recurring layer; most revenue is new-appliance volume.
Lowe's was approximately 15% of 2025 net sales and approximately 44% of year-end receivables. "Most of our products are not sold through long-term contracts."
One retailer's volume or credit event moves sales, receivables and working capital at once; no contracted revenue floor.
The United States was 10.1 billion and Brazil 2.4 billion of 2025 net sales. Management says "close to 90%" of 2025 sales were in the Americas.
Documentary Fact; Management Language for the Americas share
Brazil exposes the group to real-denominated earnings and local tax disputes; Latin American customer credit has already produced a loss.

Principal manufacturing at 20 locations in four countries: 10 in MDA North America, 8 in MDA Latin America, 1 in SDA Global, 1 other. Management says about 80% of major appliances sold in the U.S. are produced there.
Documentary Fact; Management Language for the 80% claim
Local-for-local production limits some tariff exposure but leaves fixed cost to absorb in low volume; the Supsa plant closure is under way.
Management announced a 7% price increase in MDA North America effective in Q4 and increases of up to 10% in Latin America, and describes "the largest pricing changes in a decade".
Earnings recovery relies on price realisation holding against soft demand; unproven until Q4 and 2027 results.
Management expects 2026 industry demand of about (5)% in MDA North America, 5-7% in MDA Latin America and about flat in SDA Global.
A North American decline in volume is the main drag on absorption and margin.
Gross margin fell on lower volume, higher tariff cost and cost inflation; ongoing EBIT was 97 in Q3 2026 against 180 in Q3 2025. Management targets structural cost take-out.
Documentary Fact; Management Language for take-out
Margin pressure is operational and tariff-driven, not only one-off; ongoing EBITDA for the latest twelve months is 720 (CP-1).
Capital expenditures for 2026 are expected at about 400, against 389 in FY2025.
Maintenance and product renewal spend is largely fixed, which limits cash flexibility when earnings fall.

Revenue and margin are typically highest in the third and fourth quarters. Supply chain finance obligations were 650 at September 30, 2026 (772 at December 31, 2025), with payment terms of 120 to 180 days.
Seasonal outflows in the first nine months (operating cash flow of (826) for nine months 2026, CP-1) rely on a fourth-quarter release; supplier finance sits in payables outside debt.

Brands include Whirlpool, KitchenAid, Maytag, Amana, JennAir, InSinkErator, Brastemp and Consul. The JennAir trademark was impaired by 106 in Q4 2025; JennAir, InSinkErator, Maytag and Amana remain at risk of impairment.
Large indefinite-lived intangibles (other intangibles 2,546) are a non-cash exposure and part of the ABL collateral pool (intellectual property).

The Supsa plant in Apodaca, Mexico is to close by the second quarter of 2027; costs up to about 86 impairment, 31 employee and 44 other, of which about 75 is cash. About 170 of 2026 restructuring is expected.
Documentary Fact; Management Language for timing
Adds cash outflow into 2027 while Q4 working capital release is needed for year-end net debt goals.

runs.text: Strengths. Whirlpool holds scaled, long-established appliance franchises with leading positions in the Americas and a brand portfolio including Whirlpool, KitchenAid and Maytag (Documentary Fact; Management Language for the market-position wording). It has demonstrated market access in 2026, raising USD 524 million of common equity and USD 557 million of mandatory convertible preferred in February (Documentary Fact), and it suspended the common dividend, which retains cash (Documentary Fact). After the June refinancing near-term maturities are cleared: USD 14 million falls due in the next twelve months and USD 585 million in 2028 (Documentary Fact for the 14; Analyst Interpretation for the schedule, which is rebuilt). The asset-based facility of USD 2,000 million and Brazilian facilities of USD 193 million were undrawn at September 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact). Management is executing structural cost take-out and price increases, announced at 7% in North America and up to 10% in Latin America (Management Language), and the SDA Global segment earned segment EBIT of USD 124 million on USD 710 million of nine-month sales (Documentary Fact).

Weaknesses. Leverage of 9.52x total debt over ongoing EBITDA is high and rising (Analyst Interpretation on a Documentary Fact base). Ongoing EBIT for Q3 2026 was USD 97 million against USD 180 million a year earlier and management has cut its 2026 earnings outlook twice since May (Documentary Fact; Management Language for the outlook). North American demand is soft and one retailer is about 15% of sales and about 44% of receivables (Documentary Fact). Operating cash flow is negative on a nine-month basis, and year-end net debt guidance relies on a fourth-quarter release (Analyst Interpretation). The new secured structure subordinates unsecured creditors in the collateral pool and limits flexibility through indenture covenants and a borrowing base (Documentary Fact; legal capacity Insufficient Information). Ratings are below investment grade at all three agencies and moved lower in the first half of 2026, which has reduced commercial paper access (Documentary Fact). Equity-method and other non-core assets are volatile: a USD 124 million impairment of the Whirlpool India stake was booked in Q3 2026 (Documentary Fact). Coverage of interest by ongoing EBITDA fell to 2.21x on an expense basis, and the proxy fixed charge ratio is 0.97x (Analyst Interpretation).

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The transactions that matter to creditors are these, all dated on or before the cutoff of 2026-11-05. On February 27, 2026 Whirlpool issued 11,500,000 depositary shares of its 8.50% Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock (net cash proceeds 557 million) and 7,898,550 common shares at 69 dollars per share (net cash proceeds 524 million), and used about 900 million of the proceeds to repay part of its prior revolving credit facility (10-Q Q3 pages:52-53, 57). In March 2026 it paid 157 million to buy the legal title to five assets previously held under synthetic leases (10-Q Q3 page:11). In May 2026 it amended the Long-Term Credit Agreement to cut the commitment from 3.50 billion to 2.25 billion, excluded the March 31, 2026 quarter from the interest coverage test and required a full refinancing before July 1, 2026 (10-Q Q1 page:17). In June 2026 it agreed with Arcelik to sell its remaining 25% of Beko Europe, terminate deferred rights from the 2022 Russian business divestiture and release accrued indemnities, for net cash of 84 million plus a 2.9% Arcelik stake, booking a gain of 139 million (10-Q Q3 pages:13, 46). On June 16, 2026 it issued 1,000 million of 7.500% Senior Secured Second Lien Notes due 2031 and 1,000 million of 7.875% Senior Secured Second Lien Notes due 2034 under a Rule 144A private placement, entered a new asset-based credit facility of up to 2,000 million with J.P. Morgan as agent, and terminated the Long-Term Credit Agreement; the notes and the facility share one collateral pool, first-priority for the facility and second-priority for the notes, guaranteed by domestic and Canadian subsidiaries that are ABL obligors. The proceeds and ABL borrowings repaid the 1.250% Senior Notes due 2026, the 1.100% Senior Notes due 2027 and the unsecured revolver by July 1, 2026, with 212 million of cash restricted at June 30 for that payment (10-Q Q3 pages:17-21; 10-Q Q2 page:7). The indenture limits additional debt, restricted payments, liens, investments, asset sales and mergers, requires a 101% change of control offer and may require asset-sale offers at 100% (10-Q Q3 page:18). The ABL carries a springing fixed charge coverage test of 1.00 to 1.00 when Availability falls below the greater of 10% of the Line Cap and 135 (10-Q Q3 pages:20-21). Other liquidity actions were sale-leasebacks of two assets for about 111 million in June and one for about 59 million in September, with initial annual rent of about 9 million and 5 million, and a receivables purchase agreement amended in Q3 to capacity of up to 250 million with a first-priority security interest for the purchaser in unsold program receivables (10-Q Q3 pages:11-12, 23). On July 1, 2026 it announced the Supsa plant closure. In Q3 2026 it recorded a 124 million impairment of its Whirlpool India stake and a 54 million charge on the Casas Bahia bankruptcy reorganization (10-Q Q3 pages:14, 55). The December 2025 background is the sale of about 11% of Whirlpool India for about 166 million, reducing ownership from 51% to about 40%, with deconsolidation and a gain of 251 million (10-Q Q3 page:45). Debt raised in 2026 and its effect on the debt stack and liquidity are quantified in CP-1: total debt of 6,852 million, cash of 1,103 million and undrawn committed facilities of 2,193 million at September 30, 2026. No transaction was reported after September 30, 2026 other than management statements in the October 26, 2026 release (Q4 price increases and the net debt expectation); the 10-Q Q3 reports "ITEM 5. OTHER INFORMATION None." (10-Q Q3 page:68). The executed indenture and ABL agreement are not supplied, so lien, guarantee, baskets and permitted payment terms are known only as the issuer summarises them.

fields.value: Whirlpool entered the latest quarter with weaker earnings and a much longer, more secured debt stack than a year earlier. On the company's own ongoing EBIT plus cash flow depreciation and amortization, EBITDA for the twelve months to September 30, 2026 is 720 million, down from 1,067 million in FY2025 and 1,220 million in FY2024. Total debt (notes payable, current maturities and long-term debt) was 6,852 million at September 30, 2026 against 6,520 million at December 31, 2025, so total debt over ongoing EBITDA is 9.52x against 6.11x, and net debt over ongoing EBITDA is 7.98x against 5.48x. Using the reported operating profit basis instead, the same ratios are 8.46x and 7.10x for the latest twelve months, and the direction is the same. Reported earnings were also hit in the third quarter by a 124 million impairment of the Whirlpool India equity stake and a 54 million trade customer bankruptcy charge, and flattered in earlier periods by disposal gains. The June 2026 refinancing, funded with 2,000 million of second lien notes and a 2,000 million asset-based facility that was undrawn at quarter end, removed the 2026 and 2027 euro note maturities; the sources do not print a post-refinancing maturity table, so the maturity chart below is derived. Cash from operations was negative 826 million for nine months 2026, and management's own guidance for year-end net debt requires a very large fourth-quarter working capital inflow. These conclusions are about the financial base only; interim cash interest, borrowing base availability and covenant definitions are not supplied, and every ratio here depends on the stated EBITDA definition.

fields.value: Whirlpool is a listed, widely held major and small appliance manufacturer with no sponsor named in the sources, and its recent transactions have been defensive: sell down non-core stakes, raise equity, cut distributions, and refinance bank and euro debt into secured paper. The business is concentrated in North America, which supplied most nine-month 2026 net sales of 10,467 million through MDA North America at 7,141 million, and in one retail channel, with Lowe's about 15% of 2025 net sales. Demand in North America is soft, tariffs and cost inflation are compressing margins, and management has cut its 2026 earnings outlook twice since May. The June 2026 refinancing gave the company a 2,000 million asset-based facility, undrawn at quarter end, and replaced the 2026 and 2027 euro notes with second lien notes, so near-term maturities are cleared at the cost of subordinating unsecured creditors in the collateral pool. Governance behaviour in the sources is on balance supportive of liquidity (equity issuance, dividend cuts, asset sales and sale-leasebacks) with a mixed effect on creditor ranking. The decisive unknowns are legal: what the indentures permit, what the ABL borrowing base allows, and who the large holders are, none of which is supplied. Source evidence is primary and dated, except management characterisations, which are labelled.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The transactions that matter to creditors are these, all dated on or before the cutoff of 2026-11-05. On February 27, 2026 Whirlpool issued 11,500,000 depositary shares of its 8.50% Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock (net cash proceeds 557 million) and 7,898,550 common shares at 69 dollars per share (net cash proceeds 524 million), and used about 900 million of the proceeds to repay part of its prior revolving credit facility (10-Q Q3 pages:52-53, 57). In March 2026 it paid 157 million to buy the legal title to five assets previously held under synthetic leases (10-Q Q3 page:11). In May 2026 it amended the Long-Term Credit Agreement to cut the commitment from 3.50 billion to 2.25 billion, excluded the March 31, 2026 quarter from the interest coverage test and required a full refinancing before July 1, 2026 (10-Q Q1 page:17). In June 2026 it agreed with Arcelik to sell its remaining 25% of Beko Europe, terminate deferred rights from the 2022 Russian business divestiture and release accrued indemnities, for net cash of 84 million plus a 2.9% Arcelik stake, booking a gain of 139 million (10-Q Q3 pages:13, 46). On June 16, 2026 it issued 1,000 million of 7.500% Senior Secured Second Lien Notes due 2031 and 1,000 million of 7.875% Senior Secured Second Lien Notes due 2034 under a Rule 144A private placement, entered a new asset-based credit facility of up to 2,000 million with J.P. Morgan as agent, and terminated the Long-Term Credit Agreement; the notes and the facility share one collateral pool, first-priority for the facility and second-priority for the notes, guaranteed by domestic and Canadian subsidiaries that are ABL obligors. The proceeds and ABL borrowings repaid the 1.250% Senior Notes due 2026, the 1.100% Senior Notes due 2027 and the unsecured revolver by July 1, 2026, with 212 million of cash restricted at June 30 for that payment (10-Q Q3 pages:17-21; 10-Q Q2 page:7). The indenture limits additional debt, restricted payments, liens, investments, asset sales and mergers, requires a 101% change of control offer and may require asset-sale offers at 100% (10-Q Q3 page:18). The ABL carries a springing fixed charge coverage test of 1.00 to 1.00 when Availability falls below the greater of 10% of the Line Cap and 135 (10-Q Q3 pages:20-21). Other liquidity actions were sale-leasebacks of two assets for about 111 million in June and one for about 59 million in September, with initial annual rent of about 9 million and 5 million, and a receivables purchase agreement amended in Q3 to capacity of up to 250 million with a first-priority security interest for the purchaser in unsold program receivables (10-Q Q3 pages:11-12, 23). On July 1, 2026 it announced the Supsa plant closure. In Q3 2026 it recorded a 124 million impairment of its Whirlpool India stake and a 54 million charge on the Casas Bahia bankruptcy reorganization (10-Q Q3 pages:14, 55). The December 2025 background is the sale of about 11% of Whirlpool India for about 166 million, reducing ownership from 51% to about 40%, with deconsolidation and a gain of 251 million (10-Q Q3 page:45). Debt raised in 2026 and its effect on the debt stack and liquidity are quantified in CP-1: total debt of 6,852 million, cash of 1,103 million and undrawn committed facilities of 2,193 million at September 30, 2026. No transaction was reported after September 30, 2026 other than management statements in the October 26, 2026 release (Q4 price increases and the net debt expectation); the 10-Q Q3 reports "ITEM 5. OTHER INFORMATION None." (10-Q Q3 page:68). The executed indenture and ABL agreement are not supplied, so lien, guarantee, baskets and permitted payment terms are known only as the issuer summarises them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Whirlpool is a stretched, non-investment-grade credit with a funded runway to 2028 but little earnings cushion. The strongest support is liquidity and structure: USD 1,103 million of cash and USD 2,193 million of undrawn committed facilities at September 30, 2026, equity raised in February, and only USD 14 million due within twelve months after the June refinancing. The weakest point is earnings: ongoing EBITDA for the latest twelve months is USD 720 million against total debt of USD 6,852 million, or 9.52x, with operating cash flow of negative USD 826 million for nine months and interest expense now running near USD 100 million a quarter. What decides the outcome is whether price increases and cost take-out restore North American margins, and whether year-end working capital release materialises, before the secured facility's borrowing base and its fixed charge test begin to bind.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has moved sharply the wrong way. Total debt over ongoing EBITDA was 5.43x in FY2024, 6.11x in FY2025 and is 9.52x for the twelve months to September 30, 2026, with net debt over ongoing EBITDA of 7.98x. On the stricter operating-profit basis the latest ratios are 8.46x and 7.10x, so the conclusion does not depend on which EBITDA is used. Total debt rose by USD 332 million over the first nine months of 2026 while ongoing EBITDA fell from USD 1,067 million in FY2025 to USD 720 million for the latest twelve months. The issuer does not print a leverage ratio, so every ratio here is analyst-built.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The refinancing bought time and cost carry. The June 2026 issue of USD 1,000 million of 7.500% notes due 2031 and USD 1,000 million of 7.875% notes due 2034 carries about USD 154 million of annual coupon (derived from the stated rates), replacing euro notes with coupons of 1.25% and 1.10% on about USD 1,290 million of carrying value, so roughly USD 139 million of added annual coupon before any saving on the repaid revolver. Quarterly interest expense reached USD 102 million in Q3 2026 against USD 63 million in Q2, and management guides full-year 2026 interest of about USD 350 million and Q4 interest of about USD 103 million. Ongoing EBITDA over annualised Q3 interest of USD 408 million is 1.76x, and guided full-year 2026 ongoing EBIT of about USD 293 million is 0.84x guided interest. Cash interest is not printed for the interim periods, so these are expense-based.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate on paper and uncertain in substance. Cash of USD 1,103 million and undrawn commitments of USD 2,193 million total USD 3,296 million, down from USD 4,101 million at December 31, 2025, and the nominal undrawn amount is mostly an ABL (USD 2,000 million) limited by a borrowing base the filings do not disclose. Operating cash flow was negative USD 826 million for nine months and management's guidance of about USD 700 million for the year implies a fourth-quarter inflow of about USD 1,526 million. That is a seasonal working capital release, not a trend, and it carries execution risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Covenant headroom is thin on every proxy available. The ABL tests fixed charge coverage of 1.00x only when Availability falls below the greater of 10% of the Line Cap and USD 135 million. An indicative proxy of ongoing EBITDA less capital expenditures over interest expense is 0.97x, so if availability tightened the test could bind. The proxy is not the covenant definition. The prior facility's interest coverage test of at least 3.0x was relaxed in May 2026 by excluding the first quarter, and expense-based cover has since fallen to 2.21x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditor ranking has shifted. The ABL is first lien and the Secured Notes are second lien on the same collateral pool, secured by substantially all assets of the Company and the guarantors, while about USD 4.8 billion of senior unsecured notes (derived as total debt less the Secured Notes and notes payable) remain. Whether the unsecured note indentures allowed the lien grant or required equal and ratable security is not stated and the documents are not supplied. This is an open legal question, not an adverse finding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside reported debt are material in aggregate. Supply chain finance of USD 650 million sits in payables, operating lease liabilities of USD 863 million noncurrent, a USD 575 million cumulative mandatory convertible preferred, Brazilian tax assessments (BEFIEX about USD 545 million, PIS/COFINS about USD 88 million, IPI Amnesty about USD 61 million, and USD 112 million unreserved for DIFAL), and USD 578 million of bank guarantees, letters of credit and surety bonds. None is in total debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Whirlpool holds scaled, long-established appliance franchises with leading positions in the Americas and a brand portfolio including Whirlpool, KitchenAid and Maytag (Documentary Fact; Management Language for the market-position wording). It has demonstrated market access in 2026, raising USD 524 million of common equity and USD 557 million of mandatory convertible preferred in February (Documentary Fact), and it suspended the common dividend, which retains cash (Documentary Fact). After the June refinancing near-term maturities are cleared: USD 14 million falls due in the next twelve months and USD 585 million in 2028 (Documentary Fact for the 14; Analyst Interpretation for the schedule, which is rebuilt). The asset-based facility of USD 2,000 million and Brazilian facilities of USD 193 million were undrawn at September 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact). Management is executing structural cost take-out and price increases, announced at 7% in North America and up to 10% in Latin America (Management Language), and the SDA Global segment earned segment EBIT of USD 124 million on USD 710 million of nine-month sales (Documentary Fact).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Leverage of 9.52x total debt over ongoing EBITDA is high and rising (Analyst Interpretation on a Documentary Fact base). Ongoing EBIT for Q3 2026 was USD 97 million against USD 180 million a year earlier and management has cut its 2026 earnings outlook twice since May (Documentary Fact; Management Language for the outlook). North American demand is soft and one retailer is about 15% of sales and about 44% of receivables (Documentary Fact). Operating cash flow is negative on a nine-month basis, and year-end net debt guidance relies on a fourth-quarter release (Analyst Interpretation). The new secured structure subordinates unsecured creditors in the collateral pool and limits flexibility through indenture covenants and a borrowing base (Documentary Fact; legal capacity Insufficient Information). Ratings are below investment grade at all three agencies and moved lower in the first half of 2026, which has reduced commercial paper access (Documentary Fact). Equity-method and other non-core assets are volatile: a USD 124 million impairment of the Whirlpool India stake was booked in Q3 2026 (Documentary Fact). Coverage of interest by ongoing EBITDA fell to 2.21x on an expense basis, and the proxy fixed charge ratio is 0.97x (Analyst Interpretation).

Thesis: Whirlpool can service its debt through 2027 on its liquidity, but its credit quality depends on restoring North American margins and on a year-end working capital release that its own guidance requires.
